> Not an MMO game, but rather a Motorized & Mounted Materials Organizer. I like engineering projects and study a lot, and my most used materials such as pencils, pens, erasers, rulers, sticky notes, etc. are hidden away in drawers making them annoying to get at times.  I have a hutch on my desk, and I think it would be cool to have a custom organizer and storage system that I can mount to the top or side of the hutch in order to keep it accessible and out of the way. It would be able to hold all of my most used materials and will be motorized in some places, so that I can click a button and a sticky note will dispense for instance, or the end of a ruler will eject for me to grab.

## Design

### 2026-10-13 – Started off the project nice and simple. Since I'm doing a custom mounted organizer, I started by searching for a schematic and measurements of my desk and the additional hutch/shelving that is on it,

**1h**

Started off the project nice and simple. Since I'm doing a custom mounted organizer, I started by searching for a schematic and measurements of my desk and the additional hutch/shelving that is on it, which I did find.

![Screenshot 2026-10-13 191310](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9pj7FLxKsNBBQr77R6391M1qxl1RKbJZ/98c6f14fba4f184bdd7339dd1a4a9ba66e05d9d1298d209af82709538c73afc6.png)

Next, I decided to actually decide what to include in the organizer, so I spent a bit going through my drawers and cabinets to see what I used the most and should have the best access to. It came down to various pens, pencils, markers, and dry erase markers, erasers, a ruler, sticky notes, and duct tape, because why would you not have easy access to duct tape?

I then moved onto how I would semi-automate things, and I decided to only automate a few parts. For instance, I think it would be cool to click a button and have a servo push my ruler out of a slit for me to grab, and a similar concept for my sticky notes. Even for various colored sticky notes perhaps. Depending on timeframe and complexity requirements, I may even add a way to mount my microphone arm in a better and more secure way than it is, maybe with controllability., or maybe a better lighting solution than the directional lamp I currently have pointed at the ceiling. Think about it as I write this, I actually might have to include that one just as a necessity.

![Screenshot 2026-10-13 193005](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9pj7FLxKsNBBQr77R6391M1qxl1RKbJZ/36836da207c8d81fc2a997b7c93d7c1e850088e35a9215dea75b3a6170f9f176.png)

So yeah, today was super simple and chill, but I'm sure it will pick up very quickly.

### 2026-10-15 – Another short session today, but I got a lot done. I left off last time after I made the holes for writing stationary, but they were horizontal, which means that things are more likely to fall out whe

**1h**

Another short session today, but I got a lot done. I left off last time after I made the holes for writing stationary, but they were horizontal, which means that things are more likely to fall out when bumped. So, the first task today was fixing that. I deleted the extrusion cut I did and instead made a guideline in the center of each circle at the angle and distance I wanted the whole to be. I then used the sweep tool using the guideline to make the holes the same length at an angle of -15 degrees from the horizontal. I then used the rectangular pattern tool on those features to create an array of holes.

![Screenshot 2026-10-15 163112](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9pj7FLxKsNBBQr77R6391M1qxl1RKbJZ/dcebea1a158cb86b4c08c3e0edc227267452b5161a22efc5611f57f18c54d150.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-15 163613](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9pj7FLxKsNBBQr77R6391M1qxl1RKbJZ/6e36111e11dbd2129d55429105800985fb47229e55fd51925c1e545dfe30a011.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-15 163758](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9pj7FLxKsNBBQr77R6391M1qxl1RKbJZ/93ee633729a89f0241c45ff6bd5095ef1cedbc6746ef2966506ff34ede9576e3.png)

Next, I moved onto the sticky note holder. I want it to be able to hold four colors of sticky notes, so I cut 4 slots for the sticky notes all the way through. In the back, I did the same thing as the ruler segment and cut a hole in the back to access the future servos and electronics. I also decided to add a lip at the back of the slots to ensure that the sticky notes won't accidentally go too far back in the holder.

![Screenshot 2026-10-15 165018](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9pj7FLxKsNBBQr77R6391M1qxl1RKbJZ/1cd78f0044f3a89242d7e156294ca6c4b8a5481cb34d1116d1dc2b865fe8996f.png)
